descriptionChirho: The proper name Ish-Bosheth ('man of shame'), son of King Saul who briefly reigned over Israel in opposition to David after Saul's death (2 Samuel 2-4). All 22 occurrences refer to the same individual, with sense clusters reflecting a split between the two morphemic components 'Ish' (eng: Ish, kor: 이시-, swa: Ish) and 'Boshet' (eng: Boshet, arb: إِيشْبُوشَثَ, swa: Boshethi), plus a conjunctive form 'and–for–Ish' (arb: وَلِ–إِيشْبُوشَثَ, hin: और–के–लिए–ईश–बोशेत). These are purely morphological and syntactic variants of a single proper noun.
